title: He Giveth Thee Power to Get Wealth
bigIdea: READ THE VERSE AGAIN AND NOTICE WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. IT DOES NOT SAY HE GIVES YOU WEALTH. IT SAYS HE GIVES YOU POWER TO GET WEALTH — THE GETTING IS HANDED TO YOU, AND SOMEONE WAITING TO RECEIVE IS WAITING FOR SOMETHING THIS VERSE NEVER PROMISED.

anchor.text: But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day.

benefits: Moves the verse off the poster and into the hands. The gift named is POWER TO GET — capacity, not product. A person can hold that gift for years and never open it, because they are waiting for an arrival instead of exercising a capacity.

Names the real gap without shaming anybody for it. "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children." (Hosea 4:6) Destroyed — not disadvantaged. Missing Knowledge is treated as a serious condition, and treating it seriously is the opposite of blaming the person who has it.

Gives permission to start before the Knowledge is complete. "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went." (Hebrews 11:8) He obeyed first and found out after — the order the Word actually records.

Keeps the counterweight in the same hand. "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?" (Luke 14:28) Faith moving is not faith unprepared, and a teaching that drops either verse is selling something.
inApp: The IP Register on Books -> Legal is this lesson with the poetry removed: the things this house has built, and a running count of how many are actually held. It reads zero held. Not because the work is small, but because holding what you build is a separate skill from building it — Business Systems Knowledge, which nobody is born with and most people are never taught. Open it and read the bottleneck line; it names the one thing that would move every row at once.

levels.child: HE GIVETH THEE POWER TO GET WEALTH. That means Yahweh gives you the power to GET. Read the verse slowly. "But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day." (Deuteronomy 8:18) Look at what He gives. He does not say He will hand you the money. He says He gives you the POWER to go and get it. Those are not the same thing. Think about a fishing rod. Someone gives you a rod. They did not give you a fish. They gave you the thing that catches fish. If you sit and wait for a fish to jump in your lap, you stay hungry. That is not because the gift was bad. It is because the gift was a rod. The rod works when you use it. So what if you do not know how to fish yet? That is a real problem. It is not a bad one. You were just never taught. Yahweh says that missing this hurts people. "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children." (Hosea 4:6) So you go and learn. You ask. You try. You start with what you know now. Here is a man who did that. "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went." (Hebrews 11:8) He went first. He learned on the way. You can do that too. One more thing. The wealth is for a job. The verse says He gives it so He can keep His promise. So it is never just for you. It is for what He is building.
levels.youth: HE GIVETH THEE POWER TO GET WEALTH — and the word POWER is doing all the work in that sentence. "But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day." (Deuteronomy 8:18) Notice what is actually handed over. Not wealth. The power to GET wealth. That is a capacity, and a capacity does nothing while it sits still. Somebody can believe this verse completely, quote it correctly, and still spend years waiting — because they read it as an announcement that something is coming, when it is a statement that something has already been given. Now read the verse right before it, because the two work as a pair. "And thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth." (Deuteronomy 8:17) That is what a person says when they have forgotten. And watch how verse 18 corrects it. It does not take the work away from the person. The work stays theirs — they really did get it, with their hands. What moves is the CREDIT. So when you do not know HOW — how money actually moves, how a business is formed, how a thing you made stays yours — that is not evidence you were skipped over. It is a gap in Knowledge, and the Word does not treat that gap as small. "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children." (Hosea 4:6) Destroyed. Not slowed down. So naming what you do not know is not weakness. It is agreeing with Yahweh about how serious it is, and it is the first move toward closing it. And you are allowed to begin before you understand everything. "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went." (Hebrews 11:8) He obeyed, then he found out. That order is recorded on purpose.
levels.teen: HE GIVETH THEE POWER TO GET WEALTH, and most people misread that verse in the same direction. "But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day." (Deuteronomy 8:18) They hear a promise of arrival. It is a description of equipment. There is a command hiding inside the Knowledge gap, and it is not a gentle one. "Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding." (Proverbs 4:7) GET. An imperative verb, twice. Wisdom and Understanding are not moods that descend on you when you are ready; they are things you go after. Which raises the obvious objection: if you are supposed to go get the Knowledge first, how does anyone ever start? They do not wait. "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went." (Hebrews 11:8) But hold that next to this, because both are in the same Bible and a teaching that drops either one is selling you something. "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?" (Luke 14:28) Counting the cost and going out not knowing are not opposites. The resolution is that they happen at the same time rather than in sequence: you move with the way you know right now, and you pursue what you lack while you move. Waiting until you feel qualified is not humility, and it is not caution either; it is a decision to stay where you are dressed up as patience. Nobody has ever felt qualified, and the people you admire started anyway. The last clause is the one most quotations cut off — the wealth exists so He can establish His covenant. It has a job. It is an instrument of something older than itself, which is exactly why this passage is not about getting rich.
levels.senior: HE GIVETH THEE POWER TO GET WEALTH sits inside a warning chapter, and reading it apart from that setting is how it became the most misused verse in this territory. "But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day." (Deuteronomy 8:18) The whole burden of Deuteronomy 8 is the danger of remembering wrongly once the land is good and the barns are full. "And thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth." (Deuteronomy 8:17) Notice the precision of the correction that follows. It does not answer the boast by removing the man's labour, which would have been the easier and more pious-sounding move. The labour is real and it remains his. What is relocated is the source of the power behind it. That distinction matters pastorally, because a reading that strips a person's work in order to humble them produces a different fruit than one that leaves the work and moves the credit. Then there is the matter of the gap. A man may hold this verse for decades, believe it entirely, and never exercise it — not from unbelief, but because the Business Systems Knowledge required to act on it was never handed down to him. "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children." (Hosea 4:6) Yahweh puts that at the weight of destruction, which is a kindness rather than a condemnation: He is refusing to treat as trivial what costs people their inheritance. And the last clause governs everything before it — "that he may establish his covenant" — wealth is instrumental here, never evidentiary. It is not offered as proof of favour, and its absence is not offered as proof of failure. A man who receives it and forgets the covenant has misread the chapter as badly as the man who never moved at all.

questions.q: Deuteronomy 8:18 names a gift. What exactly is given?
options: Wealth itself, as a promise to those who remember Him
Power to GET wealth — a capacity, not a product
Protection from ever losing what you have earned
questions.explain: "But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day." (Deuteronomy 8:18) The phrase is POWER TO GET. The getting remains the person's work; what is supplied is the capacity to do it. This is why waiting to receive misreads the verse — the gift was already handed over, and it was a capacity.

questions.q: Verse 17 sits immediately before it. What does it describe?
options: A person thanking Yahweh for what he has
A person saying in his heart that his own power and hand got him the wealth
A person who has lost everything and is asking why
questions.explain: "And thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth." (Deuteronomy 8:17) It is the sentence of someone who has forgotten. Verse 18 does not answer it by removing the person's labour — the labour is real and it stays his. It answers it by naming where the power came from.

questions.q: Hosea 4:6 describes what happens where Knowledge is missing. How strong is the word?
options: My people are slowed for lack of knowledge
My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge
My people are tested for lack of knowledge
questions.explain: "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children." (Hosea 4:6) Destroyed. A Knowledge gap is not treated as a minor inconvenience, which is exactly why naming your own gap out loud is not an admission of failure — it is agreeing with Him about how serious it is.

questions.q: Hebrews 11:8 says Abraham obeyed and went out. How much did he know when he went?
options: He knew the land and the route before he left
He went out, not knowing whither he went
He waited until the way was shown, then went
questions.explain: "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went." (Hebrews 11:8) Obeyed first; found out after. It is not a licence to skip counting the cost — Luke 14:28 stands in the same Bible — but it settles whether a person may start before the Knowledge is complete. Abraham did.

talkingPoints: Open by reading Deuteronomy 8:18 aloud and asking the room what is given. Most will answer "wealth." Read it again slowly and let someone catch POWER TO GET. That catch is the whole lesson and it lands better found than told.

Read verse 17 with it. The pair does something more careful than warn against pride: it leaves the labour with the person and moves only the credit. Ask what it would mean to work hard AND not say "my own hand got me this."

Bring Hosea 4:6 in as the honest naming of the gap. Ask the room, plainly, what they do not know how to do — how ownership works, how a business is formed, how a thing you made stays yours. The point is to make the gap sayable.
Then Hebrews 11:8, to give permission to begin. Ask who is waiting to feel ready, and what they would start this week if readiness were not the requirement.

Hold Luke 14:28 in the same hand so the lesson does not tip into recklessness. The resolution is that you move with what you know now AND go get what you lack — Proverbs 4:7 makes GET a command, twice.
Close on purpose, not on profit — "that he may establish his covenant" — and ask what covenant the room is building toward, letting that be the last thing said rather than the money.

lesson: HE GIVETH THEE POWER TO GET WEALTH — the gift is a capacity, the getting is yours, and faith moves before the Knowledge is complete. THE VERSE, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. "But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day." (Deuteronomy 8:18) He giveth thee POWER TO GET wealth. Not wealth. Power to get it. That is a capacity placed in a person's hands, and a capacity does nothing while it sits. Someone can hold this verse for thirty years, believe it entirely, quote it accurately, and still be waiting — because they read it as an announcement that something is coming, when it is a statement that something has already been handed over. THE VERSE BEFORE IT. "And thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth." (Deuteronomy 8:17) The correction that follows is more careful than most readings allow. It does not take the work away from the person. The work is real and it stays his — he did get it, with his hand. What moves is the CREDIT, not the labour. Yahweh supplies the power; the man swings the hammer; and the man who forgets where the power came from has not worked too hard, he has remembered too little. THE GAP IS KNOWLEDGE, NOT PERMISSION. It is a lack rather than a verdict. Permission was granted in verse 18. What is missing, for many, is Business Systems Knowledge — how ownership works, how a thing you build becomes a thing you hold. "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children." (Hosea 4:6) Destroyed, not slowed. So naming your own gap is agreement with Him about its seriousness. FAITH MOVES FIRST. "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went." (Hebrews 11:8) He obeyed, then found out. AND YOU COUNT THE COST ANYWAY. "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?" (Luke 14:28) Both are true at once. The resolution is an imperative. "Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding." (Proverbs 4:7) GET is a command. You move with what you know now, and you go get what you lack, at the same time. WHAT THE WEALTH IS FOR. The clause most quotations cut off is this: that he may establish his covenant. The wealth has a job attached. This is what keeps the passage out of prosperity doctrine — Deuteronomy 8 is a warning chapter, and wealth here is never proof of favour nor its absence proof of failure. "For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that." (James 4:15) Yahweh willing. The power is His, the getting is yours, the outcome is asked for rather than assumed.
